critical_code_review_comments: tutor_router.event_generator streams deltas including the @@META@@ footer to the client; frontend strips it via splitTutorMeta. This is fine, but if any client ever forgets to strip (e.g. a third-party consumer of the SSE endpoint), the raw JSON will leak. Consider server-side stripping the META marker from streamed deltas and emitting the parsed meta object as a separate SSE event (e.g. `data: {"meta": {...}}`). Would also let the frontend drop its manual buffering of `raw` on each message.

ai_service.build_tutor_system_prompt injects the last-8 history turns into the system message even though emergentintegrations LlmChat also tracks history by session_id. Depending on the library's semantics this may double-count context and inflate tokens on long sessions. Recommend picking one source of truth (library-managed OR manual system-prompt injection).

TutorDrawer.jsx passes `courseSlug` into streamTutor as `courseContext`, but useTutorStream.js (inline tutor) also prepends lesson title/module title into the user message. If a quiz is ever launched from InlineTutor (not currently exposed), the lesson-context wrapper prefix could confuse the quiz-mode grader. Non-blocking, but worth a comment.

The @@META@@ marker is a plaintext sentinel — if the model ever produces the literal string '@@META@@' inside an answer (unlikely but possible for a tutor teaching about prompt injection), splitTutorMeta would truncate mid-answer. Consider a more collision-resistant sentinel (e.g. a UUID prefix), or the SSE separate-event approach above.
